subject.title: fix: persist pending followup queues across gateway restart

question: Should OpenClaw advance restart followup recovery through a SQLite-backed successor and treat this JSON-sidecar PR as source context, or intentionally sponsor this branch's sidecar and system-event replay approach?
rationale: The remaining blocker is an ownership, storage, and prompt-boundary decision; automation cannot safely choose between a policy exception and a SQLite-backed recovery design.

options.title: Advance SQLite recovery
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82572 or a rebased successor as the landing path after conflicts, context persistence, and exact-head transport proof are resolved.

options.title: Sponsor this sidecar branch
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly accept the JSON sidecar, trusted replay, duplicate-replay, and stale-drop risks, but that needs a deliberate architecture decision before merge.

options.title: Pause behind broader queue API work
options.body: Wait for a broader followup/runtime API direction if durable restart recovery should be solved through a new owner boundary first.

recommendation.title: Advance SQLite recovery
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82572 or a rebased successor as the landing path after conflicts, context persistence, and exact-head transport proof are resolved.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest current-main owner signal across queue, gateway startup, and system-event surfaces that determine the safe fix shape.
